name: Turn off location for the whole PC
summary: Force the location service off for every app and account.
what: Applies the machine policy that turns location off. The Location settings page becomes read only.
benefit: No app can read where the PC is. Fewer background lookups.
risk: Low. Maps, weather, find my device and time zone auto detect stop working.
advice: Suggested for desktops that do not need location. Skip it on laptops and tablets that use maps or find my device.
facts: Applies to every account and cannot be changed in Settings afterward
The policy is documented by the vendor
Not available on Home, which ignores it

name: Stop promoted app installs and Start suggestions
summary: Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences through policy.
what: Applies the Cloud Content policy that blocks Start suggestions, post-setup app installs and promoted tiles.
benefit: No surprise sponsored apps after updates or on new accounts.
risk: None. Windows only honors this policy on Enterprise and Education, so it is hidden on Home and Pro. Use the per user version there.
advice: Suggested on Enterprise and Education. On Home and Pro use the per account version.
facts: Windows honors this policy on Enterprise and Education only
The setting is documented by the vendor

name: Stop suggestions and silent app installs (this account)
summary: Turn off tips, suggested apps and silent installs for the current user.
what: Sets the per user content delivery values that feed Start suggestions, lock screen tips and silent app installs to off.
benefit: Works on every edition, including Home and Pro, where the policy version is ignored.
risk: None. These are per account preferences and are not documented as a supported policy, so Windows can reset them after a feature update. Clarion detects that and offers to reapply.
advice: Suggested for everyone, especially on Home and Pro.
facts: Not a documented policy, so Windows may reset it after big updates
Clarion detects a reset and offers one click reapply

name: Block OneDrive file sync
summary: Stop OneDrive from syncing files without uninstalling it.
what: Applies the policy that prevents apps and features from using OneDrive for file storage.
benefit: Nothing uploads to OneDrive and it disappears from the File Explorer sidebar.
risk: Medium. Files already synced stay on the PC but stop updating. If Desktop, Documents or Pictures were moved into OneDrive, move them back first.
advice: Suggested only if you do not use OneDrive. Skip it if you do.
facts: Move Desktop, Documents and Pictures back to local folders first
Available on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop device companion app downloads
summary: Do not fetch extra vendor software and icons when a device is plugged in.
what: Applies the policy that prevents Windows from retrieving device metadata from the internet.
benefit: Fewer vendor promotions and surprise app prompts when connecting hardware.
risk: Low. Some devices show a generic icon and name.
advice: Suggested if you dislike vendor prompts when plugging in hardware.
facts: Windows will not download device names, icons and companion app hints
Applies to every account on the PC
